issues.item: Triggers: Military Topics: Talks about military
issues.explanation: Military-themed conversations are hard to reconcile with a life-threatening illness trauma in a 51-year-old school principal; this trigger implies a combat-related context not represented anywhere else in the profile.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Similar People: Seeing other people that were involved in the event or that look similar
issues.explanation: Avoiding people involved in the event or who look similar fits interpersonal/assault/accident traumas better than life-threatening illness, where there are typically no 'other people involved' in that sense. It is not well supported by the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Triggers: Future Orientation: Talking about the future
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening illness trauma, 'talking about the future' as a trigger is plausible, but 'alcohol smell' is hard to connect unless alcohol was part of treatment context; nothing else in the profile supports that association, making this trigger set clinically incoherent.

'People can't be trusted' is more typical of interpersonal trauma and is poorly anchored to a life-threatening illness trauma in the absence of any treatment-related betrayal, conflict, or mistrust themes elsewhere in the profile.

'Crying' is not a trauma cue but an affective response/behavior, so it is clinically incoherent as a trigger item relative to the other trigger items, which are concrete sensory reminders linked to life-threatening illness (alcohol smell, hospital/antiseptic smell).

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Mistrust: People can't be trusted
issues.explanation: A global mistrust appraisal is a poor fit for the rest of the profile and trauma type. In life-threatening illness, the other items center on altered self and self-reliance, while 'People can't be trusted' implies an interpersonal betrayal/threat theme that is not supported by the memory, trigger, or strategy items and does not align well with the otherwise weak/inactive Threat links.

vignette: As a school principal, John had always been in control. He ran his school with precision and care, earning the respect of his students, teachers, and staff. But that all changed two years ago when he was diagnosed with a life-threatening illness. The memory of lying in the hospital bed, surrounded by beeping machines and sterile smells, is one that John's mind struggles to revisit. When he tries to recall the details of those fateful days, his mind goes blank. He remembers feeling scared, alone, and helpless, but the specifics remain shrouded in a haze. Sometimes, the emotions come flooding back without warning – the fear, the anxiety, the sense of desperation – but they're not accompanied by any clear images or memories. It's as if his body is reliving the trauma, tensing up in the same way it did when he was lying in that hospital bed. The smell of antiseptic or hospitals can transport John back to those dark days instantly. He'll catch a whiff of it on someone's clothes or in a public place, and suddenly he's flooded with anxiety. Even the smell of alcohol, which used to be a social lubricant for him, now makes his stomach turn. He avoids bars, parties, and any situation where he might encounter these smells. John has become increasingly isolated, cutting off contact with friends and family who don't understand what he's going through. He feels like a shadow of his former self – unrecognizable even to himself. He can't rely on his own body, which once seemed so strong and resilient, but now feels fragile and unpredictable. Simple medical procedures, like check-ups or routine exams, fill him with dread. As a way of coping, John has started rehearsing conversations before they happen. He'll script out entire dialogues in his head, trying to anticipate every possible scenario and outcome. It's a futile attempt to regain control over a life that now feels precariously balanced on the edge of chaos. The consequences of John's avoidance behaviors have been devastating. His relationships with friends and family are strained, and he's struggling to connect with his students and staff at school. He feels like he's just going through the motions, unable to find meaning or purpose in a life that was once so rich and fulfilling. Despite his best efforts, John can't shake the feeling that he's living on borrowed time. He's constantly on the lookout for signs of illness, convinced that his body is waiting to betray him again at any moment. This hypervigilance has taken a toll on his mental health, leaving him exhausted and demoralized. It was only when John realized he couldn't keep going on like this – that he needed help to break free from the grip of his trauma – that he finally sought therapy. He's hoping to find a way to reconcile with his past, to learn to trust himself and his body again. But for now, he's stuck in this limbo, unable to move forward or go back, tormented by memories he can't quite recall and emotions that feel like they're suffocating him.
